citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $n\ge1$ and
$s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ to be the normed-space completion
of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ with the positive-definite norm
$q_s(u)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$ from
[[def-bessel-potential-pre-hilbert-norm-on-schwartz-space]] and
[[lem-bessel-potential-norm-is-positive-definite]].

Concretely, its elements are equivalence classes $[u_j]$ of norm-Cauchy
sequences $(u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ in Schwartz space, where
$(u_j)\sim(v_j)$ exactly when
$\lim_{j\to\infty}q_s(u_j-v_j)=0$. The metric completion carries the unique
compatible Banach-space structure supplied by
[[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]] and
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]; its norm
is $\|[u_j]\|_{H^s}=\lim_j q_s(u_j)$. The constant-sequence map
$u\mapsto[(u,u,\ldots)]$ is the canonical dense linear isometry from Schwartz
space. At this definition stage $H^s$ is an abstract completion; no
identification with a subset of $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ is implicit.

The only choice assumption is Countable Choice, used by the cited metric
completion theorem in its countable-sequence construction and completeness
argument. No full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ be the real-order Bessel-potential completion of
[[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] with its canonical embedding
$E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$
([[thm-bessel-potential-completions-embed-in-tempered-distributions]]). Write
$\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Japanese bracket, $\mathcal F$
for the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, and
$u_g(\phi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}g(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$ for the regular tempered
distribution of $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Define
$$\mathcal W_s=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n):\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu=u_g \text{ in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\text{ for some }g\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)\bigr\}.$$
Then:

1. The canonical embedding restricts to a bijection
   $E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal W_s$. Thus, after identifying a completion
   class with its image under $E_s$, $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ is **exactly** the set
   of tempered distributions whose bracket-weighted Fourier transform is the
   regular distribution of an $L^2$ class, and that class $g$ is unique.
2. The norm identity is exact:
$$\|U\|_{H^s}=\|g\|_2=\bigl\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)\bigr\|_2 \qquad(U\in H^s),$$
   where the last expression means the $L^2$ norm of the unique density $g$ of
   the distributional product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)$, and the
   defining completion norm $q_s(\phi)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat\phi\|_2$
   of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] is not renormalized.
3. The product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu$ is distributional
   multiplication of $\mathcal Fu$ by the smooth polynomially bounded bracket
   weight, not an a priori pointwise product; and $H^s$ elements are completion
   classes, not initially assumed to be functions.

Nothing here replaces the bracket weight by the Laplacian weight
$(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{s/2}$, and no pointwise value of $g$ at an individual
frequency is asserted before $g$ is obtained from the defining condition.

Assume countable choice and let $n\ge1$. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry $\mathcal F_2:L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $s\ge0$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set. Use $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ with the Bessel-potential completion convention of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Define the **restriction space**
$$H^s(D):=\{U|_D:U\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)\},\qquad \|u\|_{H^s(D)}:=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_D=u\text{ a.e. on }D\}.$$
Two extensions represent the same element exactly when their restrictions agree almost everywhere on $D$. This is the convention for fractional-order spaces on the polyhedral domain and its affine simplex cells used in the Nitsche items on this page. No $C^1$ boundary or trace theorem is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $F$ be one of its facets, and let $s>1/2$. Restriction of smooth functions has a unique bounded extension
$$T_F:H^s(K)\longrightarrow L^2(F),\qquad \|T_Fv\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_s\|v\|_{H^s(K)},$$
where $H^s(K)$ is the restriction space of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. The constant depends only on $s$ and the Fourier normalization, not on the location or orientation of the supporting hyperplane. If $V\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ is an extension of $v$, then $T_Fv$ is the restriction to $F$ of the unique $L^2$ hyperplane trace of $V$; hence it is independent of the chosen extension.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p<\infty$, and let
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex. Then restrictions of functions
smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline{\widehat S_d}$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)$ in its Sobolev norm. No density assertion for
$p=\infty$ is made.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

Let $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfy

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \varphi(x)\,dx = 1. $$

For $\varepsilon > 0$, define

$$ \varphi_\varepsilon(x) := \varepsilon^{-n}\varphi(x/\varepsilon) \qquad(x \in \mathbb{R}^n). $$

The family $(\varphi_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ is the **mollifier family
generated by $\varphi$**.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be locally integrable, let
$\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ have mass $1$, and let
$\varphi_\varepsilon$ be the associated mollifier. Then for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, the convolution

$$ (f*\varphi_\varepsilon)(x) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(y)\varphi_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy $$

is smooth, and for every multi-index $\alpha$,

$$ \partial^\alpha(f*\varphi_\varepsilon) = f*(\partial^\alpha \varphi_\varepsilon). $$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $1 \le p < \infty$ and $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$. Then

$$\|\tau_h f-f\|_p \longrightarrow 0 \qquad(h \to 0).$$

Assume countable choice (in particular, the Axiom of Choice suffices). Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $1\le p\le\infty$. Then
$L^p(\mu)$, with the norm of
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]], is
complete. Equivalently, the metric induced by that norm is a complete metric in
the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]].

Moreover, if a sequence in $L^p(\mu)$ converges in norm, then some subsequence
admits measurable representatives converging almost everywhere in the sense of
[[def-convergence-almost-everywhere-relative-to-a-measure]].

$\overline{\mu 	imes 
u}$ be the completed product of two sigma-finite
measure spaces.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, let $f\in L^1(\mathbb P)$
be real-valued, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval containing $f(x)$ for
almost every $x$, and let $\varphi:I\to\mathbb R$ be convex with
$\varphi\circ f\in L^1(\mathbb P)$. Then
$$\varphi\!\left(\int f\,d\mathbb P\right)\le\int\varphi(f)\,d\mathbb P.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim: For $U\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ and $0<s<1$, the map $(x,y)\mapsto(x,z=y-x)$ is an invertible linear $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{2d}$ with determinant of absolute value $1$. Apply the change-of-variables formula in [F6] to the nonnegative integrand, then Tonelli and Plancherel in the $x$ variable, to obtain $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{|U(x)-U(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2s}}\,dx\,dy=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\widehat U(\xi)|^2\left(\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{|e^{2\pi i\xi\cdot z}-1|^2}{|z|^{d+2s}}\,dz\right)d\xi=c_{d,s}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\xi|^{2s}|\widehat U(\xi)|^2\,d\xi.$ The inner integral is finite because its numerator is at most $C|z|^2$ near zero and at most $4$ at infinity, giving radial integrals $\int_0^1r^{1-2s}dr$ and $\int_1^\infty r^{-1-2s}dr$; it is positive for $\xi\ne0$. Rotation and dilation, each covered by [F6], give the factor $c_{d,s}|\xi|^{2s}$. The vector-valued version follows by applying this identity to each component and summing. Since $1+|\xi|^{2s}$ is comparable to $\langle\xi\rangle^{2s}$, this identifies the whole-space intrinsic norm with the Bessel norm on Schwartz functions.

We construct finitely many boundary charts. At each boundary point choose an inward direction in the interior cone of the simplex; in a sufficiently small rotated box the active facet inequalities solve for the vertical coordinate and give $t>g(x')$, where $g$ is the maximum of finitely many affine functions. Inactive facets stay away after shrinking the box. If the affine functions are $\ell_j$, then $|g(x')-g(y')|\le L|x'-y'|$ with $L:=\max_j|\nabla\ell_j|$, so $g$ is Lipschitz in this explicit sense. Compactness gives a finite cover of the boundary by smaller such boxes and one interior open set covering the remaining compact subset. Choose nonnegative smooth cutoffs $\eta_j$ supported in the corresponding larger chart sets and positive on the smaller cover. Their sum is positive on a neighborhood of the closed simplex, so $\psi_j:=\eta_j/(\sum_i\eta_i)$ there form a smooth finite partition of unity. Multiplication by each cutoff is bounded in the intrinsic norm: expand $\chi(x)w(x)-\chi(y)w(y)$ into $\chi(x)(w(x)-w(y))+w(y)(\chi(x)-\chi(y))$; the second term is bounded by $C\|w\|_2^2$ because $|\chi(x)-\chi(y)|\le\min(C|x-y|,2\|\chi\|_\infty)$ and the resulting radial kernel is integrable for $0<s<1$.

The identity extends to the completion, and that completion is exactly the $L^2$ functions with finite displayed intrinsic seminorm. For the converse density, choose smooth cutoffs $\chi_R$ equal to one on $B_R$, supported in $B_{2R}$, with $|\nabla\chi_R|\le C/R$. For any such function $W$, the difference quotient of $(1-\chi_R)W$ is the sum of $(1-\chi_R(x))(W(x)-W(y))$ and $W(y)(\chi_R(y)-\chi_R(x))$. Dominated convergence sends the first term to zero in the weighted pair $L^2$ norm; for the second, integration in $x-y$ gives at most $C R^{-2s}\|W\|_2^2$. Thus $\chi_RW\to W$ in the intrinsic norm. For compactly supported $W$, translation is continuous in $L^2$ both for $W$ and for $G_W(x,y):=(W(x)-W(y))/|x-y|^{d/2+s}$ under the simultaneous translation $(x,y)\mapsto(x-a,y-a)$. Choose a nonnegative smooth compactly supported unit-mass mollifier $\rho$. For a scalar function $Z$ and probability density $\rho_\varepsilon$, scalar Jensen gives $|\int \rho_\varepsilon(a)Z(a)\,da|^2\le\int\rho_\varepsilon(a)|Z(a)|^2\,da$. For a finite-dimensional Euclidean-valued $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)$, apply this to each real component and sum: $|\int \rho_\varepsilon Z|^2=\sum_{j=1}^m|\int\rho_\varepsilon Z_j|^2\le\sum_{j=1}^m\int\rho_\varepsilon|Z_j|^2=\int\rho_\varepsilon|Z|^2$. Applying this inequality to the scalar or vector differences for $W$ and $G_W$, then Tonelli, gives $\|\rho_\varepsilon*W-W\|_2^2+[\rho_\varepsilon*W-W]_{s,\mathbb R^d}^2\le\int\rho_\varepsilon(a)\bigl(\|W(\cdot-a)-W\|_2^2+\|G_W(\cdot-a,\cdot-a)-G_W\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^{2d})}^2\bigr)\,da.$ The right side tends to zero because both translation differences tend to zero as $a\to0$ and the mollifier supports shrink to zero. The convolution is smooth by [F5], so $C_c^\infty$ is dense. Conversely, an intrinsic-Cauchy smooth sequence has an $L^2$ limit and a weighted-pair-$L^2$ limit; an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence identifies the latter with the difference quotient of the former. Completeness and [F1] therefore identify the completion with the intrinsic space.

For a boundary-localized piece, reflect across its graph by $R(x',t)=(x',2g(x')-t)$ and set the extension below the graph to $w(R(x',t))$. The horizontal coordinates are unchanged and the vertical difference is bounded by $|t-u|+2L|x'-y'|$, so $|Rx-Ry|\le C|x-y|$; since $R^2$ is the identity, the reverse bound follows by applying the same estimate to $Rx,Ry$. Thus $R$ is bi-Lipschitz. Because $g$ is a finite maximum of affine functions, partition each integration region into the finitely many open affine pieces; their boundaries lie in finitely many hyperplanes and are null. On each piece $R$ is an affine $C^1$ diffeomorphism with determinant of absolute value $1$. Apply the nonnegative change-of-variables formula in [F6] on each such piece (and in the $y$ variable for the mixed term); Tonelli combines the resulting estimates. Consequently same-side double integrals are bounded by a constant multiple of the upper-side integral. For $x$ above and $y$ below the graph, write their heights above the graph as $a,b\ge0$. Then $a+b\le|x_d-y_d|+L|x'-y'|$, hence $|x-Ry|\le C|x-y|$; the same piecewise affine changes of variables $y\mapsto Ry$ bound the mixed integral by the upper-side seminorm. Choose chart supports with positive margin to the artificial box edges, so cross pairs for extension by zero contribute at most $C\|w\|_2^2$; the interior piece has positive distance from the simplex boundary and obeys the same bound. Sum the finitely many extensions of $\psi_jw$. The result equals $w$ on the reference simplex and is bounded in intrinsic norm.

Restricting any whole-space extension decreases both the $L^2$ norm and the nonnegative pair integral. Conversely, step 2.2 supplies a bounded extension of every intrinsic reference-simplex function; together with step 2.1 this proves equivalence of the intrinsic and restriction $H^s$ norms for $0<s<1$. Apply the whole-space Fourier hyperplane trace bound [F2] to that extension; restriction to the reference facet gives its trace, and uniqueness in [F2] identifies it with the existing trace. At $s=1$, [F4] gives on the reference simplex $\|Tw\|_F^2\le C(\|w\|_K^2+\|\nabla w\|_K^2)$ for weak $H^1$ functions; density identifies it with the restriction trace whenever the input has a whole-space extension.

Pull back by the shape-regular affine map. The map from the reference open simplex to the cell interior and its product map on the double integral are invertible affine $C^1$ diffeomorphisms. Apply the nonnegative formula in [F6] to the $L^2$ and pair-integral terms; the determinant and singular-value bounds in [F3] show that for $0<s<1$ the $L^2$ term on the reference simplex is bounded by $C h_K^{-d}\|w\|_K^2$, and its pair seminorm by $C h_K^{2s-d}|w|_{s,K}^2$: the two volume Jacobians contribute $h_K^{-2d}$ and the inverse-map distance contributes at most $C h_K^{d+2s}$. Multiplying the reference trace bound by the facet Jacobian $C h_K^{d-1}$ yields the asserted terms $h_K^{-1}\|w\|_K^2$ and $h_K^{2s-1}|w|_{s,K}^2$. At $s=1$, write $\widehat w=w\circ F_K$, where $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$. The affine weak-derivative pullback used by the scaling supplier [F3] gives $
abla_{\widehat x}\widehat w=A_K^T(
abla w)\circ F_K$. Together with [F6], its full volume-scaled norm bound is $\|
abla_{\widehat x}\widehat w\|_{L^2(\widehat K)}\le\|A_K\|\,|\det A_K|^{-1/2}\|
abla w\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^{1-d/2}\|
abla w\|_{L^2(K)}$, while $\|\widehat w\|_{L^2(\widehat K)}^2=|\det A_K|^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2$. Multiply the squared reference trace inequality of step 3.1 by the facet surface Jacobian $J_F\le C h_K^{d-1}$ from [F3]. This gives $\|T_Fw\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C J_F|\det A_K|^{-1} igl(\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\|A_K\|^2\|
abla w\|_{L^2(K)}^2 igr)\le C igl(h_K^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K\|
abla w\|_{L^2(K)}^2 igr)$. The same calculation applies componentwise to vector fields and the squared component norms add.

For $0<s<1$, the identity $\|w-w_K\|_K^2=(2|K|)^{-1}\int_K\int_K|w(x)-w(y)|^2dxdy$ and $|x-y|\le h_K$ give $\|w-w_K\|_K^2\le (2|K|)^{-1}h_K^{d+2s}|w|_{s,K}^2\le C h_K^{2s}|w|_{s,K}^2$ by [F3]. At $s=1$, apply the reference mean-zero Poincaré inequality [F4] and affine scaling [F3]. This proves the stated fractional Poincaré bound and the endpoint convention.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $s\ge0$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set. Use $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ with the Bessel-potential completion convention of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Define the **restriction space**
$$H^s(D):=\{U|_D:U\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)\},\qquad \|u\|_{H^s(D)}:=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_D=u\text{ a.e. on }D\}.$$
Two extensions represent the same element exactly when their restrictions agree almost everywhere on $D$. This is the convention for fractional-order spaces on the polyhedral domain and its affine simplex cells used in the Nitsche items on this page. No $C^1$ boundary or trace theorem is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $n\ge1$ and
$s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ to be the normed-space completion
of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ with the positive-definite norm
$q_s(u)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$ from
[[def-bessel-potential-pre-hilbert-norm-on-schwartz-space]] and
[[lem-bessel-potential-norm-is-positive-definite]].

Concretely, its elements are equivalence classes $[u_j]$ of norm-Cauchy
sequences $(u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ in Schwartz space, where
$(u_j)\sim(v_j)$ exactly when
$\lim_{j\to\infty}q_s(u_j-v_j)=0$. The metric completion carries the unique
compatible Banach-space structure supplied by
[[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]] and
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]; its norm
is $\|[u_j]\|_{H^s}=\lim_j q_s(u_j)$. The constant-sequence map
$u\mapsto[(u,u,\ldots)]$ is the canonical dense linear isometry from Schwartz
space. At this definition stage $H^s$ is an abstract completion; no
identification with a subset of $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ is implicit.

The only choice assumption is Countable Choice, used by the cited metric
completion theorem in its countable-sequence construction and completeness
argument. No full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ be the real-order Bessel-potential completion of
[[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] with its canonical embedding
$E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$
([[thm-bessel-potential-completions-embed-in-tempered-distributions]]). Write
$\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Japanese bracket, $\mathcal F$
for the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, and
$u_g(\phi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}g(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$ for the regular tempered
distribution of $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Define
$$\mathcal W_s=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n):\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu=u_g \text{ in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\text{ for some }g\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)\bigr\}.$$
Then:

1. The canonical embedding restricts to a bijection
   $E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal W_s$. Thus, after identifying a completion
   class with its image under $E_s$, $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ is **exactly** the set
   of tempered distributions whose bracket-weighted Fourier transform is the
   regular distribution of an $L^2$ class, and that class $g$ is unique.
2. The norm identity is exact:
$$\|U\|_{H^s}=\|g\|_2=\bigl\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)\bigr\|_2 \qquad(U\in H^s),$$
   where the last expression means the $L^2$ norm of the unique density $g$ of
   the distributional product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)$, and the
   defining completion norm $q_s(\phi)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat\phi\|_2$
   of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] is not renormalized.
3. The product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu$ is distributional
   multiplication of $\mathcal Fu$ by the smooth polynomially bounded bracket
   weight, not an a priori pointwise product; and $H^s$ elements are completion
   classes, not initially assumed to be functions.

Nothing here replaces the bracket weight by the Laplacian weight
$(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{s/2}$, and no pointwise value of $g$ at an individual
frequency is asserted before $g$ is obtained from the defining condition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $F$ be one of its facets, and let $s>1/2$. Restriction of smooth functions has a unique bounded extension
$$T_F:H^s(K)\longrightarrow L^2(F),\qquad \|T_Fv\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_s\|v\|_{H^s(K)},$$
where $H^s(K)$ is the restriction space of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. The constant depends only on $s$ and the Fourier normalization, not on the location or orientation of the supporting hyperplane. If $V\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ is an extension of $v$, then $T_Fv$ is the restriction to $F$ of the unique $L^2$ hyperplane trace of $V$; hence it is independent of the chosen extension.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge2$, $1/2<s\le1$, and a shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For $0<s<1$ and a scalar or vector-valued function $w$ on a cell $K$, define
$$|w|_{s,K}^2:=\int_K\int_K\frac{|w(x)-w(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2s}}\,dx\,dy;$$
for $s=1$ set $|w|_{1,K}:=\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)}$ (componentwise for vectors). For every cell $K$, facet $F\subset\partial K$, and $w\in H^s(K)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]], the trace from [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]] satisfies
$$\|T_Fw\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K^{2s-1}|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr).$$
For $0<s<1$, the norm $\bigl(\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr)^{1/2}$ is equivalent on a fixed reference simplex to the restriction $H^s$ norm. At $s=1$ the displayed estimate is the weak $H^1$ trace inequality; no additional identification of the full intrinsic weak-$H^1$ space with a restriction space is asserted. Constants are uniform over the shape-regular family and depend only on $d,s$ and its shape bound.

For every $w\in H^s(K)$, with cell mean $w_K:=|K|^{-1}\int_Kw$, the same conventions give
$$\|w-w_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^s|w|_{s,K}.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p<\infty$, and let
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex. Then restrictions of functions
smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline{\widehat S_d}$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)$ in its Sobolev norm. No density assertion for
$p=\infty$ is made.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex and let
$G\in C^1(\overline K;\mathbb R^d)$. If $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit
normal on each facet $F$, then
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$
For an orientation-preserving affine map $F_K(\widehat x)=b+A\widehat x$,
the oriented area element transforms as
$$n_{K,F}\,dS=\det(A)A^{-T}\widehat n_{\widehat F}\,d\widehat S.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an affine bijection from a bounded open
set $\widehat K\subset\mathbb R^d$ to $K$, where $A$ is invertible, and let
$1\le p\le\infty$. For every integer $r\ge0$ and scalar
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$, the pullback $\widehat v:=v\circ F$ belongs to
$W^{r,p}(\widehat K)$. For $r\ge1$ its first weak derivatives satisfy
$$D_{\widehat x_j}\widehat v=\sum_{i=1}^d A_{ij}(D_{x_i}v)\circ F,$$
and higher derivatives are obtained by applying this constant-matrix rule
repeatedly. In particular, for each $0\le m\le r$,
$$|\widehat v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat K)}\le C(d,m)\|A\|^m|\det A|^{-1/p}|v|_{W^{m,p}(K)},$$
where $|\det A|^{-1/p}:=1$ for $p=\infty$. The reverse estimate holds
with $A^{-1}$ and $|\det A|^{1/p}$ in place of $A$ and
$|\det A|^{-1/p}$.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The underlying coordinate index set of $\mathbb R^d$
is $I_d=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$. In this definition the conventional labels
$1\le i\le d$ are relabeled by $i\mapsto i-1$: write
$\widehat x_i:=\widehat x(i-1)$, and let $e_i\in\mathbb R^d$ be the function
on $I_d$ with $e_i(i-1)=1$ and $e_i(k)=0$ for $k\ne i-1$.
The vertex and barycentric labels $0,\ldots,d$ are distinct from these
underlying coordinate indices. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Suppose
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ vanishes almost everywhere outside a compact
set $K_0\subset\Omega$. Let $E_0u$ denote the extension of a representative of
$u$ by zero to $\mathbb R^n$, and for $|\alpha|\le k$ let
$E_0(D^\alpha u)$ denote the extension by zero of the corresponding
derivative representative. Then
$$E_0u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad D^\alpha(E_0u)=E_0(D^\alpha u)\quad\text{almost everywhere, }|\alpha|\le k,$$
and every $L^p$ component norm is preserved:
$$\|E_0(D^\alpha u)\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|E_0u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
so that $\|E_0u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$. The case
$k=0$ is included, and complex scalars are handled by the same bilinear
pairing.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

Let $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfy

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \varphi(x)\,dx = 1. $$

For $\varepsilon > 0$, define

$$ \varphi_\varepsilon(x) := \varepsilon^{-n}\varphi(x/\varepsilon) \qquad(x \in \mathbb{R}^n). $$

The family $(\varphi_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ is the **mollifier family
generated by $\varphi$**.

An **$L^1$ approximate identity** on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a family
$(K_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ of functions in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, where

$$\|K_\varepsilon\|_1:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|K_\varepsilon(x)|\,dx,$$

such that:

1. $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} K_\varepsilon(x)\,dx = 1$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$;
2. there is $M < \infty$ with $\|K_\varepsilon\|_1 \le M$ for every
   $\varepsilon > 0$;
3. for every $\delta > 0$,
   $$ \int_{|x|>\delta} |K_\varepsilon(x)|\,dx \longrightarrow 0 \qquad(\varepsilon \to 0^+). $$

This is the general notion used later for both compactly supported mollifiers
and the Gaussian family.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $(K_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ be an $L^1$ approximate identity on
$\mathbb{R}^n$. If $1 \le p < \infty$ and $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, then

$$\|f*K_\varepsilon - f\|_p \longrightarrow 0 \qquad(\varepsilon \to 0^+).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be locally integrable, let
$\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ have mass $1$, and let
$\varphi_\varepsilon$ be the associated mollifier. Then for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, the convolution

$$ (f*\varphi_\varepsilon)(x) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(y)\varphi_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy $$

is smooth, and for every multi-index $\alpha$,

$$ \partial^\alpha(f*\varphi_\varepsilon) = f*(\partial^\alpha \varphi_\varepsilon). $$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ be nonnegative with
$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\rho=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$.
For $\varepsilon>0$ put $\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$
and
$$\Omega_\varepsilon=\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^n\setminus\Omega)>\varepsilon\},\qquad\Omega_\varepsilon=\mathbb R^n\ \text{when }\Omega=\mathbb R^n .$$
Then $\rho_\varepsilon*u$ is defined and smooth on $\Omega_\varepsilon$, and
for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le k$,
$$D^\alpha(\rho_\varepsilon*u)=\rho_\varepsilon*(D^\alpha u)\qquad\text{on }\Omega_\varepsilon,$$
as pointwise smooth functions for the constructed representatives and as
almost-everywhere classes. Here $D^\alpha u$ is extended by zero off $\Omega$
in the convolution.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the compactly supported smooth
functions $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$$\|\varphi-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}<\delta.$$
No such norm-density assertion is made for $p=\infty$.

Assume countable choice (in particular, the Axiom of Choice suffices). Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $1\le p\le\infty$. Then
$L^p(\mu)$, with the norm of
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]], is
complete. Equivalently, the metric induced by that norm is a complete metric in
the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]].

Moreover, if a sequence in $L^p(\mu)$ converges in norm, then some subsequence
admits measurable representatives converging almost everywhere in the sense of
[[def-convergence-almost-everywhere-relative-to-a-measure]].

Assume Countable Choice. For every $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, weighted
Fourier transformation extends from Schwartz space to a surjective linear
isometry
$$J_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^n),\qquad J_s([u_j])=\lim_{j\to\infty}\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(u_j)$$
in $L^2$. If $g=J_s([u_j])$, then
$$E_s([u_j])=\mathcal F^{-1}(u_{\langle\xi\rangle^{-s}g})$$
where $u_h$ denotes the functional $\phi\mapsto\int h(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$
whenever this integral defines a tempered distribution. This is a well-defined
continuous linear injection
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ for both weak and strong dual
topologies. It sends the canonical Schwartz class to its usual regular
distribution and is independent of the representing Cauchy sequence.

Assume Countable Choice.  Let $u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ and
$\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$.  Then

$$\mathcal F(u*\varphi)=(\mathcal Fu)(\mathcal F\varphi), \qquad \mathcal F(\varphi u)=(\mathcal F\varphi)*(\mathcal Fu).$$

In the second formula the convolution means
$(\mathcal Fu)*(\mathcal F\varphi)$ under the distribution-first convention.
If $v\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ has compact support, then

$$\mathcal F(u*v)=(\mathcal Fu)(\mathcal Fv).$$

Here $\mathcal Fv$ is the smooth polynomially bounded function representing
the transform of the canonical tempered extension of $v$.  No product of two
arbitrary distributions and no convolution of two arbitrary tempered
distributions occurs.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Choose a whole-space extension $Q\in H^r(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$ of $q$, componentwise by [F1]. For $a$ in the interior of $K$ and $0<t<1$, set $A_t x=a+t(x-a)$. For every Schwartz vector field, the affine change-of-variables formula in [F5] and dominated convergence give $Q\circ A_t\to Q$ in $H^r(\mathbb R^d)$ as $t\uparrow1$; the dilation operators are uniformly bounded for $1/2\le t\le1$ because their Fourier norm is $t^{-d}\int\langle t\xi\rangle^{2r}|\widehat Q(\xi)|^2d\xi\le2^d\|Q\|_{H^r}^2$. Density of Schwartz space in the Bessel completion extends this convergence to every $Q$.

Let $f_0$ be the zero extension of $\operatorname{div}q$ from $K$ to $\mathbb R^d$. Strong continuity of affine dilations in $L^2$, first for smooth compactly supported functions and then by density and the uniform change-of-variables bound in [F5], gives $t f_0\circ A_t	o f_0$ in $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$. Since $A_t(\overline K)$ is compactly contained in $K$, there is a bounded open neighborhood $N_t\supset\overline K$ with $A_t(N_t)\subset K$. On $N_t$, $Q\circ A_t=q\circ A_t$ almost everywhere, because [F5] sends the null set where $Q$ and $q$ differ to a null preimage under the invertible affine map. This divergence identity follows directly without assuming that $q$ has all first weak derivatives in $L^2$: for $\phi\in C_c^\infty(N_t)$ put $\psi=\phi\circ A_t^{-1}\in C_c^\infty(K)$. Apply [F5] to the positive and negative parts of each integrable component product and use $
abla\phi=t(
abla\psi)\circ A_t$ to obtain $\int_{N_t}(Q\circ A_t)\cdot
abla\phi=t^{1-d}\int_Kq\cdot
abla\psi=-t^{1-d}\int_K(\operatorname{div}q)\psi=-\int_{N_t}t(\operatorname{div}q)\circ A_t\,\phi$. Thus $\operatorname{div}(Q\circ A_t)=t(\operatorname{div}q)\circ A_t$ distributionally.

For fixed $t<1$, let $q_{t,\epsilon}:=\rho_\epsilon*(Q\circ A_t)$ for a nonnegative smooth unit-mass mollifier supported in the unit ball. Since $Q\circ A_t\in H^r\subset\mathcal S'$ and $\rho_\epsilon\in\mathcal S$, [F6] gives $\widehat{q_{t,\epsilon}}=\widehat{Q\circ A_t}\,\widehat{\rho_\epsilon}$. Nonnegativity and unit mass give $|\widehat{\rho_\epsilon}(\xi)|\le1$, while its defining integral and dominated convergence give $\widehat{\rho_\epsilon}(\xi)\to1$ for each $\xi$. The exact weighted Fourier characterization in [F1] and dominated convergence therefore give $q_{t,\epsilon}\to Q\circ A_t$ in $H^r(\mathbb R^d)$. Choose $N_t$ bounded with $\overline K\subset N_t$ and $A_t(N_t)\subset K$, as in step 2.1, and put $f_t:=t(\operatorname{div}q)\circ A_t\in L^2(N_t)$. If $\epsilon<\operatorname{dist}(\overline K,N_t^c)$, then for $x\in K$ the convolution kernel $y\mapsto\rho_\epsilon(x-y)$ is supported in $N_t$. Differentiating the smooth convolution under the integral and using the distributional identity $\int_{N_t}(Q\circ A_t)\cdot\nabla\phi=-\int_{N_t}f_t\phi$ with $\phi(y)=\rho_\epsilon(x-y)$ gives, componentwise and after summing, $\operatorname{div}q_{t,\epsilon}(x)=-\int_{N_t}(Q\circ A_t)(y)\cdot\nabla_y\rho_\epsilon(x-y)\,dy=\int_{N_t}f_t(y)\rho_\epsilon(x-y)\,dy$. Extend $f_t$ by zero from $N_t$ to $\mathbb R^d$; [F5] gives $\rho_\epsilon*f_t\to f_t$ in $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$, so these divergences converge to $f_t$ in $L^2(K)$. Choose $t_n\uparrow1$ and then sufficiently small $\epsilon_n$ so that $q_n:=q_{t_n,\epsilon_n}$ is smooth and $q_n\to q$ in $H^r(K)$ while $\operatorname{div}q_n\to\operatorname{div}q$ in $L^2(K)$, using steps 1.1 and 2.1 for the two limits. The countable selection is permitted by [A1].

For a smooth $v$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline K$, apply the classical affine-simplex Gauss–Green formula [F3] to each smooth field $q_n v$. The volume terms converge because $q_n\to q$ in $L^2(K)$ and $\operatorname{div}q_n\to\operatorname{div}q$ in $L^2(K)$; the facet terms converge because the $H^r$ trace in [F1] is continuous for $r>1/2$. This proves the displayed identity for such smooth $v$.

For arbitrary $v\in H^1(K)$, affine pullback of the published smooth-density result in [F2] gives smooth $v_m\to v$ in $H^1(K)$. The volume integrals in the identity for $v_m$ converge by $L^2$ Cauchy–Schwarz, and their facet traces converge in $L^2(F)$ by the endpoint estimate in [F2]. Passing to the limit proves the identity for every $H^1$ test.

For the global case, take a whole-space extension $U\in H^{1+r}(\mathbb R^d)$ of $u$; [F1]'s Fourier multiplier bound gives $
abla U\in H^r(\mathbb R^d)$. Thus both cell traces of $
abla u$ on an interior facet are restrictions of the same hyperplane trace, so they agree as vectors and their opposite outward normals cancel. For a global $w\in H^1(\Omega)$, its two value traces agree on each interior facet: on every compact subfacet choose a ball whose closure lies in $\Omega$ and meets no other facets, multiply $w$ by a smooth cutoff equal to one near that subfacet, extend by zero, and mollify with radii tending to zero below the cutoff margin. [F5] applied to the cutoff function and its weak gradient, with the interior derivative-commutation identity, gives convergence of these smooth approximants in $H^1$ on the smaller neighborhood. Their traces therefore converge on each cell by [F2], while the smooth approximants have identical restrictions from both sides. Exhaust the facet by compact subfacets; its lower-dimensional rim has surface measure zero. Sum the first identity over all cells with $q=
abla u$ and test $w$. The interior fluxes cancel by the common vector trace and the interior test traces agree; the volume divergence is $\Delta u=-f$. Rearranging gives the global formula.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $s\ge0$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set. Use $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ with the Bessel-potential completion convention of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Define the **restriction space**
$$H^s(D):=\{U|_D:U\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)\},\qquad \|u\|_{H^s(D)}:=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_D=u\text{ a.e. on }D\}.$$
Two extensions represent the same element exactly when their restrictions agree almost everywhere on $D$. This is the convention for fractional-order spaces on the polyhedral domain and its affine simplex cells used in the Nitsche items on this page. No $C^1$ boundary or trace theorem is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $n\ge1$ and
$s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ to be the normed-space completion
of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ with the positive-definite norm
$q_s(u)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$ from
[[def-bessel-potential-pre-hilbert-norm-on-schwartz-space]] and
[[lem-bessel-potential-norm-is-positive-definite]].

Concretely, its elements are equivalence classes $[u_j]$ of norm-Cauchy
sequences $(u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ in Schwartz space, where
$(u_j)\sim(v_j)$ exactly when
$\lim_{j\to\infty}q_s(u_j-v_j)=0$. The metric completion carries the unique
compatible Banach-space structure supplied by
[[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]] and
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]; its norm
is $\|[u_j]\|_{H^s}=\lim_j q_s(u_j)$. The constant-sequence map
$u\mapsto[(u,u,\ldots)]$ is the canonical dense linear isometry from Schwartz
space. At this definition stage $H^s$ is an abstract completion; no
identification with a subset of $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ is implicit.

The only choice assumption is Countable Choice, used by the cited metric
completion theorem in its countable-sequence construction and completeness
argument. No full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ be the real-order Bessel-potential completion of
[[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] with its canonical embedding
$E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$
([[thm-bessel-potential-completions-embed-in-tempered-distributions]]). Write
$\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Japanese bracket, $\mathcal F$
for the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, and
$u_g(\phi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}g(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$ for the regular tempered
distribution of $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Define
$$\mathcal W_s=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n):\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu=u_g \text{ in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\text{ for some }g\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)\bigr\}.$$
Then:

1. The canonical embedding restricts to a bijection
   $E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal W_s$. Thus, after identifying a completion
   class with its image under $E_s$, $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ is **exactly** the set
   of tempered distributions whose bracket-weighted Fourier transform is the
   regular distribution of an $L^2$ class, and that class $g$ is unique.
2. The norm identity is exact:
$$\|U\|_{H^s}=\|g\|_2=\bigl\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)\bigr\|_2 \qquad(U\in H^s),$$
   where the last expression means the $L^2$ norm of the unique density $g$ of
   the distributional product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)$, and the
   defining completion norm $q_s(\phi)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat\phi\|_2$
   of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] is not renormalized.
3. The product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu$ is distributional
   multiplication of $\mathcal Fu$ by the smooth polynomially bounded bracket
   weight, not an a priori pointwise product; and $H^s$ elements are completion
   classes, not initially assumed to be functions.

Nothing here replaces the bracket weight by the Laplacian weight
$(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{s/2}$, and no pointwise value of $g$ at an individual
frequency is asserted before $g$ is obtained from the defining condition.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge2$, $1/2<s\le1$, and a shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For $0<s<1$ and a scalar or vector-valued function $w$ on a cell $K$, define
$$|w|_{s,K}^2:=\int_K\int_K\frac{|w(x)-w(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2s}}\,dx\,dy;$$
for $s=1$ set $|w|_{1,K}:=\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)}$ (componentwise for vectors). For every cell $K$, facet $F\subset\partial K$, and $w\in H^s(K)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]], the trace from [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]] satisfies
$$\|T_Fw\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K^{2s-1}|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr).$$
For $0<s<1$, the norm $\bigl(\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr)^{1/2}$ is equivalent on a fixed reference simplex to the restriction $H^s$ norm. At $s=1$ the displayed estimate is the weak $H^1$ trace inequality; no additional identification of the full intrinsic weak-$H^1$ space with a restriction space is asserted. Constants are uniform over the shape-regular family and depend only on $d,s$ and its shape bound.

For every $w\in H^s(K)$, with cell mean $w_K:=|K|^{-1}\int_Kw$, the same conventions give
$$\|w-w_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^s|w|_{s,K}.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The underlying coordinate index set of $\mathbb R^d$
is $I_d=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$. In this definition the conventional labels
$1\le i\le d$ are relabeled by $i\mapsto i-1$: write
$\widehat x_i:=\widehat x(i-1)$, and let $e_i\in\mathbb R^d$ be the function
on $I_d$ with $e_i(i-1)=1$ and $e_i(k)=0$ for $k\ne i-1$.
The vertex and barycentric labels $0,\ldots,d$ are distinct from these
underlying coordinate indices. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex, let $\widehat P$ be a finite
dimensional $\mathbb K$-space of polynomial functions on it, let
$\widehat F$ be any facet, and let integer $m\ge0$. For $1\le p,q\le\infty$ there is a finite
constant $C$ such that
$$|v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat S_d)}+\|v\|_{L^p(\widehat F)}\le C\|v\|_{L^q(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$
For every pair of integers $0\le m\le\ell$, there is also a finite
constant $C$ such that
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)} \le C|v|_{W^{m,q}(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$
For finitely many facets, one constant works for all of them. In particular,
every linear degree-of-freedom functional on $\widehat P$ is bounded with
respect to the $L^q(\widehat S_d)$ norm.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded
polyhedral open set $\Omega$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let $v$ be a
real-valued scalar member of the conforming piecewise-polynomial space in
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Then $v\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$.
Its weak gradient agrees almost everywhere on each cell with the ordinary
cellwise polynomial gradient.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ have a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and let $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ have the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]] and [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]. For every boundary facet $F\subset\partial K$ there is a bounded affine-simplex trace map $T_{K,F}:W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)\to L^2(F;\mathbb R)$ agreeing with classical restriction on smooth functions. If $w\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, then $T_{K,F}(w|_K)=0$ in $L^2(F;\mathbb R)$. In particular, any globally $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ function that is polynomial on each cell and belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ has zero classical boundary restriction on every boundary facet.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected polyhedral open set, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Fix a polynomial degree $k\ge1$. Let $V_h$ be the real scalar conforming polynomial space of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], viewed as a subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]], and let $Y_h:=V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, where $H^1_0$ is the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; [[lem-nitsche-h-one-zero-functions-have-zero-facet-traces]] proves its facet-trace consequence. Boundary facets form $\mathcal F_h^\partial$. If $F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial$, let $K_F$ be its unique incident cell, $n_F$ its outward unit normal, $|F|$ its $(d-1)$-dimensional measure, and set $h_F:=|K_F|/|F|>0$. For functions with a defined boundary normal trace write $\partial_n v:=\nabla v\cdot n_F$ on $F$.

Let $\mathcal X_h$ consist of $v\in H^1(\Omega)$ such that for every cell $K$ there is $s_K>1/2$ with $v|_K\in H^{1+s_K}(K)$. By [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $v$ has an $L^2(F)$ trace on each facet, and each component of $\nabla(v|_K)$ is in $H^{s_K}(K)$, hence has an $L^2(F)$ trace by the same lemma; the derivative mapping follows from $|\xi_j|\langle\xi\rangle^{s_K}\le\langle\xi\rangle^{1+s_K}$ in the Bessel-potential norm. Thus $\partial_n v$ and all displayed integrals are defined. In particular, $V_h\subseteq\mathcal X_h$ and the exact/adjoint functions in the later regularity hypotheses lie in $\mathcal X_h$. For a dimensionless penalty coefficient $\gamma_0\ge0$ and symmetry parameter $\theta\in\{0,1\}$, define the same bilinear formula on $\mathcal X_h\times\mathcal X_h$:
$$a_h^\theta(v,w):=\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v)w\,dS-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fv(\partial_n w)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fvw\,dS.$$
For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ and boundary data $g$ with the displayed integrals finite, define
$$\ell_h^\theta(w_h):=\int_\Omega f w_h\,dx-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fg(\partial_n w_h)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fg w_h\,dS.$$
The **nonsymmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^0$; it has the consistency flux in the trial slot only. The **symmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^1$; it has both transposed consistency fluxes. The discrete weak-boundary problem is the standard Nitsche method when $\gamma_0>0$: it seeks $u_h\in V_h$ such that $a_h^\theta(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h^\theta(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. This extension makes expressions such as $a_h^\theta(u,w_h)$ and $a_h^\theta(e,\zeta-z_h)$ well-defined when the exact and adjoint functions have the stated cellwise regularity. The boundary penalty is $\gamma_0/h_F$; $h_F$ is the cell-face height divided by $d$, not the face diameter. The zero value $\gamma_0=0$ is used only for the penalty-free algebraic comparison.

The energy seminorm and the comparison seminorm used below are
$$\|v\|_{E,h}^2:=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2,\qquad \|v\|_{\#,h}^2:=\|v\|_{E,h}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
These expressions are used only on functions for which their volume and facet traces are defined. The parameter $\theta$ fixes the sign convention; no convention based on a reciprocal small stabilization parameter is implicit.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\eta\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. For
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$, suppose that for every $\gamma\le\alpha$ there is
$v_\gamma\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$D^\gamma u=v_\gamma$ weakly. Then $\eta u$ has a weak $\alpha$-derivative,
and its almost-everywhere class is
$$D^\alpha(\eta u)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}(D^\beta\eta)D^{\alpha-\beta}u\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
where $D^\beta\eta$ is the classical derivative and products are pointwise
products of representatives. The resulting class does not depend on the
representatives.

For $k\in\mathbb N_0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, if
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and $D^\beta\eta\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ for
every $|\beta|\le k$, then $\eta u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and the same
formula holds in $L^p$ for every $|\alpha|\le k$. In particular,
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is a sufficient condition on the
multiplier for this global conclusion.

For $\Omega=\varnothing$ all classes are zero and the identity holds. The
pairing convention is bilinear, with no complex conjugation.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Suppose
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ vanishes almost everywhere outside a compact
set $K_0\subset\Omega$. Let $E_0u$ denote the extension of a representative of
$u$ by zero to $\mathbb R^n$, and for $|\alpha|\le k$ let
$E_0(D^\alpha u)$ denote the extension by zero of the corresponding
derivative representative. Then
$$E_0u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad D^\alpha(E_0u)=E_0(D^\alpha u)\quad\text{almost everywhere, }|\alpha|\le k,$$
and every $L^p$ component norm is preserved:
$$\|E_0(D^\alpha u)\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|E_0u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
so that $\|E_0u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$. The case
$k=0$ is included, and complex scalars are handled by the same bilinear
pairing.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

Let $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfy

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \varphi(x)\,dx = 1. $$

For $\varepsilon > 0$, define

$$ \varphi_\varepsilon(x) := \varepsilon^{-n}\varphi(x/\varepsilon) \qquad(x \in \mathbb{R}^n). $$

The family $(\varphi_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ is the **mollifier family
generated by $\varphi$**.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,

For each cell $K$, let $b_K$ be its centroid, let $m_K:=|K|^{-1}\int_K\zeta$, and let $g_K:=|K|^{-1}\int_K
abla\zeta$. Define the affine polynomial $p_K(x):=m_K+g_K\cdot(x-b_K)$ and set $A_K:=|
abla\zeta|_{s,K}$, where at $s=1$ this is the cell $L^2$ norm of the weak Hessian. The mean of $\zeta-p_K$ is zero and the mean of its gradient is zero. The mean-zero fractional Poincaré estimate [F2] applied to $
abla\zeta$ gives $\|
abla(\zeta-p_K)\|_K\le C h_K^sA_K$; ordinary mean-zero Poincaré applied to $\zeta-p_K$ then gives $\|\zeta-p_K\|_K\le C h_K^{1+s}A_K$.

We record the required vertex-star geometry. The solid angle of every shape-regular cell at any vertex is at least $c(d,\sigma)>0$: the inscribed ball has radius at least $h_K/\sigma$, its center is at distance at most $h_K$ from the vertex, and rays through that ball contain a spherical cap of radius bounded below in terms of $\sigma$. Disjoint cell interiors give disjoint solid-angle interiors, so at most $N(d,\sigma)$ cells meet at a vertex. In the spherical link of a vertex, facet adjacency is adjacency of cells across a facet containing that vertex. At an interior vertex the link is the full sphere. Its cell-adjacency graph is connected: for $d=2$ the link is a circle divided into arcs; for $d\ge3$, each codimension-two-or-higher link face has dimension at most $d-3$, and the directions of endpoints whose chord from a fixed generic direction meets that face lie in its radial cone, of spherical dimension at most $d-2<d-1$. A finite union of these forbidden sets has measure zero, so choose an intermediate direction outside the forbidden sets for two generic endpoints and join them by two projected chord segments. The resulting path avoids the lower-dimensional skeleton and crosses only facet interiors, proving graph connectivity. At a boundary vertex, every connected component of the graph contains a boundary facet incident to the vertex. Otherwise a path from a cell-interior direction in that component to any generic direction cannot leave the component: each crossing is through a link facet, and the assumed absence of an exposed facet gives a neighboring cell in the same component. Thus every generic direction belongs to that component; its finite closed link is the full sphere, and the finitely many incident simplices then contain a whole ball about the vertex, making it interior, a contradiction. Any shortest path in a component has at most $N-1$ edges; shape regularity makes diameters comparable across each shared facet, so all cells on such a path have diameters comparable by a uniform constant.

Let $I_{h,0}\zeta$ be the continuous piecewise-affine function with these nodal coefficients. Exhaust the relative interior of $F$ by the compact sets $E_m:=\{x\in F:\operatorname{dist}_F(x,\partial F)\ge1/m\}$, omitting empty sets; each lies in $F\cap\Omega$ by the matching-mesh convention, and the omitted facet rim has surface measure zero. The boundary of the fixed polyhedral domain lies in finitely many supporting hyperplanes $P_1,\ldots,P_m$. Choose any whole-space extension $Z\in H^{1+s}(\mathbb R^d)$ of $\zeta$. Its distributional derivative has Fourier multiplier $2\pi i\xi_j$; hence by [F3], $|2\pi\xi_j|\langle\xiangle^s\le2\pi\langle\xiangle^{1+s}$ and $\|
abla Z\|_{H^s}^2:=\sum_{j=1}^d\|\partial_j Z\|_{H^s}^2\le(2\pi)^2d\|Z\|_{H^{1+s}}^2$. For each $P_j$, choose $d$ affinely independent points in that plane and a point off it to form a nondegenerate simplex having a facet in $P_j$; this only names the plane trace in [F2] and imposes no mesh condition. Apply the scalar Fourier hyperplane trace estimate in [F2] to every component $\partial_k Z$ and sum the finitely many squared inequalities. After a rigid coordinate change this gives the componentwise vector trace and $\|T_{P_j}
abla Z\|_{L^2(P_j)}^2:=\sum_{k=1}^d\|T_{P_j}(\partial_k Z)\|_{L^2(P_j)}^2\le C_s\|
abla Z\|_{H^s}^2$.

Group the boundary facets by their supporting planes.
